en: The Hymn to Guhyeśvarī: O Blessed One, of manifold forms, changeless, stainless, whose every form is uncaused, whose nature transcends all determination!
O Goddess, I bow to Your pair of lotus feet, which transcend all the Vedas and possess an eternally imperishable nature. || 1 ||

Your smiling moon-like face becomes the night with its moonlight, while at midday your face rises like the sun with its thousand rays; the splendor of your reddened countenance appears both at sunrise and at the time of sunset.
O Goddess, I bow to your pair of lotus feet. || 2 ||
In the regions of her throat and belly are the three worlds of heaven, earth, and the netherworld;
the entire host of celestial bodies are her teeth; the trees are the lines of hair upon her body; and her hips, red and white, are like mountains and oceans.
O Goddess, I bow to your pair of lotus feet. || 3 ||
The winds and fires are your very inhalations and exhalations;
through their closing and opening, they constitute the times of dissolution and creation.
Your [eyes], possessing twelve suns and terrifying mouths—
O Goddess, I bow to your pair of lotus feet. || 4 ||
O Goddess, as Your divine essence— which is the quintessence of all the Vedas— pervades Your slender body on every side,
Your mind turns toward revealing the entirety of the three worlds.
O Goddess, I bow to your pair of lotus feet. || 5 ||
Those gods who face the ritual procedures are your servants standing at your feet;
O pure one whose intellect is held in the crown, all paths indeed belong to you.
How then can I describe your greatness, O secret goddess?
O Goddess, I bow to your pair of lotus feet.
He who, full of devotion, recites this hymn at the conclusion [of the ritual] during worship,
his intellect becomes clearly enlightened;
he attains a lofty abundance of devotion toward the Mother of all beings.
They come under the power of the palm of one's hand and obtain success and nourishment. || 7 ||
The Guhyeśvarī Stotra, composed by Mañjunātha and extracted from the Śrī Svayaṃbhū Purāṇa, is complete.
